clue.text: Tries tucking in top of trouser suit

indicators.note: the word for tries folds a letter into its middle, as a shirt is tucked in

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court, so tries means hears

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to tuck a shirt into the waistband of a trouser suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is the legal sense: a judge hears a case. 'Suit' looks like clothing but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Became agitated about banker's ultimate squeeze

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter taken from the next word
agitated letters are stirred up into a new order
the ultimate letter of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: Someone grew flustered over a financier's final crunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges BECAME into EMBACE; 'about' puts it round R, the last letter of banker's.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze someone can mean to hug them tightly, a synonym for an embrace.

clue.text: Valued time invested in costly reversal

indicators.note: one letter is put money-like into the other word, placed inside it
the word for costly is turned so it reads from right to left

parts.note: something costly is dear

explanation.surface: A financial picture: time spent on a pricey investment that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' turns DEAR into RAED; T is 'invested in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valued has been assessed or rated at a certain worth.

clue.text: Suspect everybody returned during term as planned

indicators.note: the reversed word sits within the rearranged letters, as an event inside a period
letters that are planned are arranged in a new order
the word for everybody comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: A teacher has doubts as everyone came back mid-term as scheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges the letters of two clue words; 'returned' turns the everybody word round, and 'during' sets it inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is amiss is the idiom meaning to sense trickery or deceit.

clue.text: Carpet expert must be in contact

indicators.note: one word has to go inside the other

parts.note: to contact someone is to reach them
a pro is an expert, short for professional

explanation.surface: A specialist in rugs needs to stay in touch with clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is British slang for giving them a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet an employee is to scold them, a synonym of rebuking them.

clue.text: Polished broadcast of discovery by engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word for discovery is taken by its sound

parts.note: a find is a discovery

explanation.surface: A slick radio report of a breakthrough made by engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: FINED is pronounced like FIND; 'by' only places RE beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polished is elegant and cultivated, a synonym for refined manners.

clue.text: Road up after parking — that's punitive

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed road word comes after the letter for parking

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A road being dug up after a parking dispute feels like a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal means relating to punishment, so a penal measure is a punitive one.

clue.text: Exercises incorporated into speech surgery

indicators.note: the short abbreviation is built into the middle of the longer word

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Drills built into a talk on how a surgeon works.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a single piece of surgery carried out on a patient.

clue.text: Dress some cut off

indicators.note: off here means wrong or awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A tailor takes some fabric off a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, and dress can mean clothing worn for an occasion.

clue.text: Blood group, say, identifies such a clumsy individual

parts.note: B is one of the blood groups, alongside A, AB and O
to say is to utter
to finger someone is to identify them to the police

explanation.surface: Your blood type supposedly reveals that you are a clumsy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one statement, but it splits into three pieces after 'Blood group' and 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps dropping things is called this, as if their hands were greasy.

clue.text: Instrument chap left at home after party

indicators.note: the left and at-home letters are placed after the party word, so they come second

parts.note: a chap is a man
a do is a party
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man stays home after a party to play music.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a lute-like stringed musical instrument that is plucked.

clue.text: Settle a guest's alliance

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the phrase has the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A host making a visitor comfortable, as if forming an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across settLE A GUEst.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a union of parties or nations joined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Beneficiary gets to keep fine European cow

indicators.note: the word for beneficiary holds the two letters within it

parts.note: an heir is a beneficiary of a will
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An heir inherits a fine European cow in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet had a calf.

clue.text: Story from newspaper covering light beer

indicators.note: the newspaper's two letters wrap round the word for light

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
airy means light
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A news report on light beer, like an article about a brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale is a traditional children's story full of magic.

clue.text: Turns down ranges after the Christmas period

indicators.note: the word for ranges comes after the month abbreviation

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, the month of Christmas
lines are ranges, as of products

explanation.surface: A shopper rejects product ranges once the festive season is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer is to turn it down or refuse it.

clue.text: Facade of indifference for a feature of the weather?

indicators.note: a front of indifference puts the facade word second, after the word it belongs to

parts.note: cold means indifferent or aloof
a front is a facade, a false outward show

explanation.surface: An aloof manner described as if it were a weather system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facade of indifference' reads as one phrase but gives its two words in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold front is the leading edge of a cooler air mass on a weather map.

clue.text: Glove mostly carried by a theologian is allowed

indicators.note: the trimmed glove word is held inside the other letters

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a mitten is a glove

explanation.surface: A cleric carrying most of a glove is let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the glove word's last letter; 'carried by' puts the rest between the two Ds of the theologian, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted means let in or permitted, a synonym of allowed, past tense matching.

clue.text: Makes use of lad to support raffle

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits underneath the other

parts.note: a draw is a raffle
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy helps out at a fundraising raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on resources is to make use of them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Doctor had to be overwhelmed

parts.note: had means owned or possessed

explanation.surface: A physician had to be swamped by work.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowned can mean swamped or submerged, as a sound drowned by noise is overwhelmed.

clue.text: Hang around, discarding last two bits of underwear

indicators.note: the final pair of letters is thrown away from the word for underwear

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: Someone loiters while throwing away bits of their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay around longer than needed, a synonym of loiter.

clue.text: Warning from French of exploding grenade?

indicators.note: an exploding word is blown apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A French cry of alarm as a grenade goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the French fencing call warning an opponent to get ready.

clue.text: Professional women wearing coat

indicators.note: the letter for women is wrapped in the coat word, as if dressed in it

parts.note: a coat of paint is a layer

explanation.surface: A businesswoman in a coat, dressed for the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer is a member of one of the classic learned professions.

clue.text: Cyclist's answer ignored by attacker

indicators.note: the attacker word leaves out the letter for answer

parts.note: a raider is an attacker

explanation.surface: A bike rider's reply goes unheeded by a mugger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cyclist's' means cyclist is, so the definition is just Cyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist is someone who rides a bicycle, so is a rider.

clue.text: Away leg unavailable to the audience

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
a stage is a leg of a journey

explanation.surface: A football away fixture that the crowd can't watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening offstage takes place out of sight of the theatre audience.

clue.text: Like some rivers — boy, it's up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone at a riverbank shouts that the water level has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAD and IT together: LADIT read bottom-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers with estuaries rise and fall with the sea's ebb and flow.

clue.text: Instruction from substitute with good system

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute
order means system or arrangement

explanation.surface: A deputy hands down a directive for a well-run system.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is a regular payment instruction given to a bank.

clue.text: Concluded popular female made a mistake

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A well-liked woman got something wrong and drew conclusions.
explanation.definitionFit: To have concluded something is to have deduced it from evidence.

clue.text: Ploughman's row about lines

indicators.note: the row word goes round the doubled letters

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
L is a line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A rural row between farmhands about planting lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' means a line of seats, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tills the soil with a plough is one who cultivates the land.
